svg.title: CineApp — application map

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: Version 8.54.2 · 2026-10-13 · one page, eight zones, from the widest view to the finest
Every box names the file, route or function that carries it, so the map doubles as an index into the code. Reasons live in DOC-TECH.md, DECISIONS.md and CLAUDE.md.
Vector drawing: zoom freely. Self-hosted media front end — Next.js App Router, React, TypeScript, SQLite — over Jellyfin, Radarr, Sonarr, Jellyseerr, qBittorrent, Bazarr, Jackett.

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: Device, reverse proxy, container, upstream services

Everything a viewer sees goes through src/proxy.ts; nothing in the browser talks to an upstream service directly, and only a television fetches without a session cookie. Configuration and secrets live in data/ beside the database (app setting → .env → default), so a fresh install needs
no .env. One container, one writable volume (./data): SQLite, logs, image cache, reports, generated secrets.

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: Choosing a path, and the remux pipeline — src/lib/webcodecs/
Every file — Matroska or MP4 — is read over HTTP byte ranges and repackaged in the tab as fragmented MP4 for MediaSource. No pixel and no copied audio sample passes through
JavaScript: the remuxer only rewrites the packaging. Audio that cannot cross MediaSource is decoded in the tab (TrueHD and AAC in WebAssembly) and re-encoded. A refusal is always a
named string, which the activity page groups by, and the server player is its answer.

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: what the box names is where it lives in the code
database, log file, browser storage, cache
each outgoing arrow is labelled with its answer
a place (browser, container) or a family of files
solid: happens on the normal path
dotted: a push, a fallback, a background task, a hint
the label says what travels, or when
solid arrow: a call · dashed: its answer
Start at zone 1 for the whole system, then follow a viewer: the interfaces (2), the
native player (3) and its safety net (4), one playback end to end (5), what is
cached where (6), what is written down (7), and what the gate lets through (8).
Boxes named « section 3 » or « 3b » refer to zones 3 and 4.

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: Cinema (/) and Management (/gestion), the bridge between them, sign-in and the first-launch assistant (/setup)

Two roles, admin and user. Hiding the administration group and the management link is presentation only: a user who types /gestion gets pages whose reads answer 403 (ADMIN_ONLY_READS, zone 8). Every cinema screen is a field of the address hash, so Back steps out one screen at a time; desktop and phone are two layouts sharing one function per decision (DECISIONS.md). Sheets are wired by the sheet lifecycle: useSheetMorph, useDelayedClose, arrivedByBack read once at mount, usePointerCapture, and cinemaClose as the only way out.

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: The safety net behind the native path, and the only path to a television
The server player plays what the native path refuses, what a slow link cannot carry and what goes to a television. Jellyfin decides between DirectPlay, DirectStream and Transcode; every
byte still goes through the application’s relay. A MediaSource stream cannot leave the tab, so a television always gets the server’s stream: the page becomes a remote control (Chromecast)
or hands its element’s route over (AirPlay), and the server keeps the resume point when the page goes quiet.
4a · The server player and the slow connection

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: From « Lire » to the session summary
One session id joins every line of a playback; a rebuild rewrites start under the same id. A page killed by iOS sends its summary at the next launch (why: lost), and a
position Jellyfin never received leaves through unsentPosition. resumeAt: 0 means from the beginning; an absent resumeAt means ask the server.

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: SWR, the device cache, the server cache
The cinema opens on what the device kept, then the network corrects it. The catalogue is frozen on purpose (it changes daily); only the resume and next-up feeds follow focus. While a film fills
the screen SWR is paused, which is why the player’s own queries carry playerBootstrapOptions and why closing the player revalidates explicitly. A paused query is dropped, not deferred.

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: Which line goes where, and who reads it — data/logs/
Player line kinds: opening, start, fallback, network, rebuild, error, seek, stall, audio, pause, cast, reserve, subtitle-gen, fluidite, stop. Every native and server
line carries session and build; incident lines carry timeline, and stall/stop carry diag.*. Bench and dev lines never reach player.log, so they never count as a

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: src/proxy.ts, the single gate — cast passes, roles, blocked tags

The interface never enforces a permission: src/proxy.ts refuses whatever a user should not do, and a television is the only caller allowed in without a session — for one title, and only for the stream and its subtitles. x-session-expired: 1 is emitted by the proxy alone, so a bare 401 from an upstream service is never mistaken for the viewer’s own session ending.

text.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
